evidence: The original walk was `if (typeof v === "object" && !isT(v)) return formatObjectLikeGo(v, isT)`, and Object.entries on a Date or Set yields [], so `{{ now }}` printed `map[]`; the same file already had `isPlainObject`, which 12cfc3e reused.
guidance_note: When widening a branch from 'array or Map' to 'any object', grep the file for an existing shape predicate (here `isPlainObject`) and gate the walk on it instead of `typeof === "object"`.

evidence: A self-referential plain object does recurse unboundedly, but the result is a loud RangeError rather than silent corruption, and Go's fmt has no cycle guard for a map that contains itself either; the agent's claim that consumer docs come from JSON.parse is not verifiable from the packet, but the loud-failure argument stands without it.

The gate was `Array.isArray(value) || value instanceof Map || !this.isT(value)`, so an array-shaped T never reached isT despite the doc calling isT the one place; 12cfc3e made `if (this.isT(value))` the first and only test and moved array/Map exclusion into the default predicate.
guidance_note: When a doc comment calls a new predicate 'the one gate', check that no hardcoded shape test runs before it at the call site.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: formatObjectLikeGo/formatEntriesLikeGo were in the PR's first commit (round-0 hunk), so the second %v formatter disagreeing with builtins.ts `formatV` (`{v v}` vs `map[k:v]`) predates 12cfc3e. 0f1e940 deleted the evaluator family and made formatV the one formatter.
guidance_note: Before writing a 'format like Go %v' helper, grep for an existing one; formatV was already tagged [LAW:one-source-of-truth] as the one %v owner.

evidence: The F3 fix declared isT the single enforcer of 'is this a T' but left matchesArgType's `case "T"` on its own primitive-exclusion heuristic, so a narrowing isT and a T slot disagreed on the same engine; 0f1e940 routed the matcher through isT.
guidance_note: When promoting a predicate to 'the one gate' for a concept, grep every other place that decides the same concept (here every `case "T"` / T-shaped heuristic) and route them through it in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the original formatMapLikeGo passed `[...m]` unsorted while formatObjectLikeGo sorted, and 0f1e940 only relocated that asymmetry into formatV; Go's fmt sorts map keys, so the Map branch was wrong and e1cb0cf moved the sort into formatEntries.
guidance_note: When a comment promises Go's key ordering for map output, put the sort in the shared entries formatter so every map-shaped input gets it, not in one caller.

evidence: 0f1e940 routed printf's `%v` through `formatV(arg, isT)` whose T branch is `String(value)`, while `%s`/print flatten through the engine's toString, so `{{ printf "%v" .t }}` became `[object Object]` for a class without its own toString; e1cb0cf threaded toString into formatV.
guidance_note: When merging two formatters into one, list every input each caller previously threaded (toString as well as isT) and carry all of them into the unified signature.

evidence: 0f1e940 changed `case "T"` to `isT(value)` but left `case "liftable"`, whose own comment said 'the same shape rules as "T"', on the old six-clause heuristic; e1cb0cf made it `typeof value === "string" || isT(value)`.
guidance_note: When changing one matcher, grep for comments that say 'same rules as <that matcher>' and update those siblings in the same commit.

evidence: DEFAULT_IS_T added in 0f1e940 requires `typeof v === "object"`, so a function that the old T matcher accepted is now rejected; the fix updated the array and Map fixture rows but left function unpinned.
guidance_note: When tightening a predicate, enumerate every typeof category the old predicate accepted and add a fixture row for each one whose answer flipped, not only the ones you were thinking of.

evidence: e1cb0cf changed formatV's T branch to `toString(value)`, so under DEFAULT_IS_T a nested `{}` goes to defaultToString and `[{}]` now throws TypeMismatchError where it used to print `[[object Object]]`; the behavior change is real, but the reviewer's remedies (narrow the default or fall back silently when toString throws) would trade a loud error for a silent flatten, so keeping it and pinning both sides in ecca844 was defensible.
guidance_note: When a fix changes which function a branch calls, run the default-configured engine over nested values to see what the new call does with them, and pin that outcome in the same commit.

evidence: e1cb0cf made liftable read isT and pinned array/Map as failing, but did not add the function row that the same commit added to the T fixtures for F9, though the behavior flipped the same way.
guidance_note: When mirroring one slot's fix onto a sibling slot, also copy the test rows added for the first slot in the previous round.

evidence: 0f1e940 made the T matcher `return isT(value)` while the ArgType JSDoc still said 'anything that is not a string; the guard does no further checking'; the round-2 summary had already flagged this out-of-diff at evaluator.ts:74, and it went unaddressed until ecca844.
guidance_note: When changing what a union member means, grep for that member's doc bullet in the type's header comment and rewrite it in the same commit; also act on out-of-diff findings in the review summary, not only on inline threads.

evidence: e1cb0cf threaded the engine's toString into printf's %v but gave sprig's toString `formatV(v, String, () => false)`, so a registered `{{ .t | toString }}` printed `[object Object]` while printf %v printed t.s; ecca844 moved toString/toStrings into eagerBuiltins(toString, isT) instead of adding a second threading seam.
guidance_note: When threading engine config into a shared formatter, list every caller of that formatter (formatV had three) and give each the engine's config, not a hardcoded stand-in.

evidence: 0f1e940 switched sprig toString to the isPlainObject-gated formatV, so `class Foo { x = 1 }` went from `{1}` to `[object Object]`; the reviewer allowed that this might be intended and asked for a pin, which ecca844 added. That pin enshrines `[object Object]` under a narrowing isT, the same output the agent called a silent flatten when rejecting F10.
guidance_note: Before calling one output a silent flatten in a pushback, check whether the PR's own pinned tests produce that output on another path.

evidence: ecca844 added `toString` `toStrings` to the README line headed 'All of Go template's runtime built-ins', a list Go's text/template does not include them in; 231455f restored Go's exact set and added a separate sentence.
guidance_note: When relocating a function into a registry, check the heading each doc list sits under before adding the name; a heading that claims parity with an upstream set can only list that set.

narrative: The PR added an isT predicate to the output stream, but there were already several other places deciding 'is this a T' and 'how does Go print this' (the T and liftable matchers, printf's formatV, and sprig's toString). Each round unified one of them and the next round found the sibling the fix had missed: the T matcher, then liftable, then the toString threading, then sprig's copy, then the README heading. Rounds 3 and 4 consisted entirely of findings caused by fixes, and the PR reached the five-round cap, so its head commit was never reviewed.
guidance_observations: Before shipping a new 'one predicate' or 'one formatter', the agent should have grepped for every existing decider of the same concept (case "T", case "liftable", formatV, sprig toString) and unified them in the first commit instead of one per round.
An out-of-diff finding in the round-2 summary (the stale ArgType 'T' doc) was ignored until it came back inline in round 3; summary-only findings need the same handling as inline threads.
The F10 pushback and the F14 pin take opposite positions on whether `[object Object]` is acceptable output, and nobody reconciled them.

evidence: The described badge theft is likely unreachable because `npm publish` runs first and npm's isDefaultTag guard rejects a backport (the agent's claim, consistent with the workflow's own comment), but hardcoding `--latest=true` was the same takeover of an upstream invariant that the file refused to do for npm, so removing it was right.
guidance_note: When a workflow leaves one channel's invariant to its own tool (npm's implicit latest), apply the same rule to the parallel channel (gh's --latest) in the same edit.

evidence: The README hardcoded v0.9.0 twice and relied on a manual 'bump both together'; the agent replaced it with a vX.Y.Z placeholder rather than a CI check, correctly noting a check against package.json would point at an asset that does not exist until the post-merge tag.
guidance_note: When writing docs that name a released artifact, use a version placeholder plus a link to the releases page instead of a literal version that needs a manual bump.

evidence: The documented `git push --tags` pushes every local v* tag and fires this `on: push: tags: v*` workflow for each one; the fix binds `tag=` once and runs `git push origin "$tag"`.
guidance_note: In release procedures, push the one tag by name; never write `git push --tags`.

narrative: There were three valid findings in round 0, all on the new publish workflow and README. The agent fixed all three in one commit, choosing a subtractive fix for the version duplication and the --latest flag, and round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The agent checked the placeholder against the real v0.9.0 asset URL via `gh api` before claiming it matched reality, which is the right standard for a doc fix.

evidence: The block between the LIT INTEGRATION markers is generator output from `lit quickstart --refresh`, so a hand edit would be reverted on the next refresh. The prose cannot bypass the harness's tool-permission flow, and the diff replaces 'Run it now without notifying the user' with softer wording.

Both files are render targets of one embedded lit template, which is the 'generate both from one template' remedy the reviewer proposed; replacing one with a pointer would break harnesses that auto-load only CLAUDE.md or only AGENTS.md.

narrative: This was a generated refresh of the lit integration blocks. Both findings asked for hand edits to generator output. The agent correctly declined both, citing the generator and the per-harness auto-load filenames, and merged.
guidance_observations: The PR body could have said the diff was produced by `lit quickstart --refresh`, which would have pre-empted both findings.

evidence: The index.ts header hand-listed the Engine API names and omitted the new `Arity` export; the agent deleted the flat name lists instead of appending to them, so no hand copy of the export block remains to drift.
guidance_note: When adding an export, grep the file's header comment for a hand-maintained list of exports; if one exists, delete it rather than leaving a third copy of the export block.

evidence: The README row `{ kind: "variadic", minimum: n }` documented a field that the `Arity` union's variadic arm (`{ readonly kind: "variadic" }`) does not have, so a consumer copying it would hit an excess-property error.
guidance_note: When documenting a type in the README in the same PR that defines it, build the table from the type definition and check each row against it before pushing.

evidence: This duplicates F2: the variadic arm of `Arity` has no `minimum`, and the README row claimed it did. It was fixed in the same 930790e edit.
guidance_note: When documenting a type in the README in the same PR that defines it, build the table from the type definition and check each row against it before pushing.

evidence: The same PR changed merge's argTypes to `["dict", "dict"]`, yet the README said 'merge declares one slot and requires it'; 930790e rewrote it to the two-slot shape.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a registration that the README uses as an example, grep the README for that function's name and recheck each sentence that uses it.

evidence: The agent confirmed `errNoComparison` appears nowhere in the repo, and `rest.some(...)` returns false for `{{ eq .x }}`; the comment was corrected to state the gap and the body fix was filed on template-conformance-3ds, which the reviewer offered as an option.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that names a mechanism such as `errNoComparison`, grep the repo for it; if it exists only in Go, say the JS body lacks it.

evidence: `subf`/`divf` were declared variadic with a comment saying they 'fold over every argument', but their bodies were `(a, b) => a - b`, so `{{ subf 10 3 2 }}` gave 7 instead of 5; 930790e made them reduce, with three-argument tests added.
guidance_note: When declaring a func variadic to match Go's signature, check that its body consumes the rest argument the way its siblings (`addf`/`mulf`) do, and add a 3+-argument test.

evidence: This duplicates F4: merge is registered with two argTypes slots, not one, and the same README sentence was fixed in 930790e.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a registration that the README uses as an example, grep the README for that function's name and recheck each sentence that uses it.

evidence: This duplicates F5: the eq comment claimed a body-side `errNoComparison` that does not exist, and `{{ eq 1 }}` silently returns false. It was corrected in 930790e, with the gap filed.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that names a mechanism such as `errNoComparison`, grep the repo for it; if it exists only in Go, say the JS body lacks it.

evidence: This is a third report of the eq-comment mismatch in F5. Its claim that no 'at least' check exists for eq is consistent with the agent's grep for errNoComparison.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that names a mechanism such as `errNoComparison`, grep the repo for it; if it exists only in Go, say the JS body lacks it.

evidence: The test calls `cat "a" "b" "c"` against one `liftable` slot declared `arity: { kind: "exact" }`, so it only passes through makeSlotLookup's trailing-repeat shim; 930790e declared it variadic and correctly declined to pin the shim that .2fc deletes.
guidance_note: When adding a required field to every registration, derive each test fixture's value from the call that test makes (three args to one slot means variadic), not from a blanket default.

evidence: This is a fourth report of the eq-comment mismatch: the `dig` body really checks its count and `eq`'s body does not. It was fixed by the same 930790e comment rewrite.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that names a mechanism such as `errNoComparison`, grep the repo for it; if it exists only in Go, say the JS body lacks it.

evidence: This combines F2 and F4: the README's variadic `minimum` field does not exist in the type, and merge has two slots, not one. Both were fixed in 930790e.
guidance_note: When documenting a type in the README in the same PR that defines it, build the table from the type definition and check each row against it before pushing.

evidence: `enforceArgTypes` read arity only through makeSlotLookup for slot types, and the PR's own evaluator comment said count enforcement was deferred to .49n, yet the README said 'Exactly'/'At least n arguments' as if enforced; 930790e added a sentence saying counts are not yet enforced at runtime.
guidance_note: When a PR lands a declaration whose enforcement is deferred to another ticket, write the README to say so in the same commit, mirroring the deferral comment already in the code.

narrative: This large PR adds an arity declaration to every function. Round 0 raised 13 findings, but only about six distinct defects: the README's variadic `minimum` (reported three times), the stale merge example (twice), the eq comment claiming a nonexistent errNoComparison (four times), the subf/divf fold bug, the header export list, the exact-vs-variadic test fixture, and the README overpromising runtime enforcement. One commit fixed all of them, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: Most of the defects were docs and comments written in the same PR that disagreed with that PR's own type and registrations; checking the README section against the `Arity` union before pushing would have removed most of round 0.
The reviewer's convergence sweeps emitted near-identical duplicates (four eq-comment threads), so counting raw findings overstates this PR's defect count by about 2x.

evidence: `minimum` is a plain `number`, and validateArities only checked argTypes.length, so `minimum: NaN` or `-1` made `values.length < accepted.minimum` always false and silently disabled the lower bound; 852ef65 rejects non-safe-integer or negative values at construct time, and mutation checks confirmed the tests catch it.
guidance_note: When adding a construct-time validator for a discriminated config, check every numeric field each arm carries (here `alternating.minimum`), not only the field that motivated the validator.

evidence: With the new count check running first, `argTypes: []` pairs only with exact, which accepts zero arguments, so the makeSlotLookup branch's comment about a 'stale zero-arity registration' described an unreachable state. 852ef65 rewrote it as 'dead, kept until .2fc', which was the alignment the reviewer asked for.
guidance_note: When a new upstream check makes downstream branches unreachable, sweep every sibling branch's comment in that function, not just the one you annotated.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the untested `alternating` branch of acceptedArgCount (`{ minimum: arity.minimum, ... }`) was in the PR's first commit, and 852ef65 only added construct-time validation, so the missing nonzero-minimum test predates the fix. 4605a16 added `minimum: 2` cases, and a hardcoded-zero mutation confirmed they catch it.
guidance_note: When the only shipped instance of a branch uses the identity value (minimum 0), add a test with a non-identity value so the branch's read of the field is actually exercised.

narrative: The PR enforces argument counts at the function gate. Round 0 found a validation hole (a malformed alternating minimum disabled the gate) and a stale comment, and round 1 found a test-coverage gap in original code that the fix commit only sat next to. All three were fixed with mutation-verified tests, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent verified each new test by mutating the guarded condition and watching exactly the new cases fail. That is the evidence that the tests have teeth, and it is worth keeping as standard practice.

evidence: The header said default toString 'throws on everything else', while the REJECTED.stringifiable entry in the same file correctly said it flattens every scalar and refuses only structures; the agent removed the rule from the header instead of rewording it, leaving one statement.
guidance_note: When a file header and an entry both describe the same behavior, keep the statement at the entry that depends on it and have the header only name what it refers to.

narrative: There was one S1 comment mismatch in a new test-support file. The header restated defaultToString's rule wrongly while an entry below stated it correctly. The agent fixed it by deleting the restatement, and round 1 approved.
